caption_en: 71. Room (p): wall E, with decoration of the fourth style, cuts the floor of cocciopesto decorated with black and white tesserae (see fig. 64), datable to the Republican age.
72. Room (p): on jamb E (with mixed opus masonry) the decoration of the fourth style has a black plinth adorned with plants; in the red middle area edges of carpet in semicircles.

73. Room (p), N wall, section E: black plinth (panel with plans); yellow middle area (panel with semicircular carpet edges). The fourth style decoration of this room had simple vignettes with animals.

74. Environment (p). In front of wall E, decorated in the fourth style, with panels with plants in the high black plinth and, in the middle area, a central yellow panel and red side panels separated by architectural views, the cocciopesto floor relating to a room later abolished is visible. The carpet edges of the side panels continue on those of the adjacent walls, so as to give the impression that large panels enclose the entire room as a unit.
75. Room (p), wall E, section N: panel with plan in the black plinth; edges of carpet in semicircles in the yellow panel of the middle area. IV style.
76. Room (p), wall E, section S: the partition with corolla that closes the architectural foreshortening of the middle area. IV style.

77. Room (p), S wall with IV style decoration: panels with plants in the black plinth; yellow central panel and red side panels separated by architectural glimpses with candelabra in the middle area; discolored upper area; stucco frame. The circular window takes light from the peristyle (k) of the adjoining house (IX 5, 14-16).
79. Room (p), wall O with the holes in which the beams of the floor were housed: remains of decoration of the IV style. 79 N53124
78. Room (p), S wall, section E: in the stucco frame, the palmettes alternate with unusual shells. IV style.

1. The old photo reproduces the imperial age layout of the atrium (b), with the impluvium covered with molded marble slabs, in which two marble fountain supports rest; behind the impluvium is the table, with lion-pawed peacock supports and a breccia top; in the background the tablinum (1) and the peristyle (N); the decoration of the fourth style of the side walls is also visible. DAIR 2188
2. Atrium (b), wall E with remains of fresco of the fourth style; in the N panel of the wing (h) was the vignette reproduced in fig. next.
3. The vignette depicting Spring that adorned one of the panels in the middle area of the atrium (b).

4. Atrium (b), wall E: in the S section of the door of (i) the IV style decoration of the plinth can be distinguished. In the red panel, under a mask hanging from a double-arched garland, are scaled carpet edges.
5. Atrium (b), wall O, section N: edges of a carpet in circles in the yellow middle area. IV style.
6. Atrium (b), overall view from E: in the S panel of the wing (e) was the vignette with Spring, and edges of a turned ribbon carpet, visible in the old photo in fig. l.
8. Atrium (b): the table supports, in pavonazzetto in the shape of lion's paws, end with a palmette; the plane is of breccia (S side). 79 N52077
7. Atrium (b): table supports, in pavonazzetto in the shape of lion's paws, end with a palmette; the top is of breccia (N side).

9. Room (c), wall N: the masonry, on which the remains of a functional cladding of the fourth style rest, with a high red plinth with panels, is in uncertain work with brick heads in the lower part; the upper part, in which the rectangular window overlooking the Via di Nola opens, is in brick curtain and mixed work.
10. Room (c), wall E with masonry in opus incerta and brick heads (towards the façade) and mixed work (towards the atrium); remains of a tall red hoof.
12. Room (c), wall O with masonry in opus incerta and brick head (towards the façade). The tall red paneled plinth reveals a service function for this rather large room.
11. Room (c), S wall, section W of the door open onto the atrium: masonry in opus incerta with mixed opus heads, wall cladding with high red plinth.

13. Room (d), wall N. Decoration of the fourth style: plinth and plinth are black (the plinth is made of panels with a vase in the centre and shoots on the sides); the middle area has a red central panel with a painting and carpet borders and white side panels with vignettes; in the upper area there are figures within architecture.
14. Room (d), wall N, section O: in the black plinth there is a panel with a branch. IV style.
15. Room (d), N wall, section O: remains of a cartoon with cupid. IV style.
16. Room (d), N wall, central section: black panel with large vase. IV style.
17. Room (d), wall E, section to the N of the door open to the atrium: black plinth; middle area with carpet edge panel. IV style.
18. Room (d), wall E, section S: black plinth; middle area with carpet edge panel. IV style.
19. Room (d), S wall with remains of the IV style decoration: in the central panel there was a painting depicting Ariadne abandoned (H, 1224).
20. Room (d), S wall, section O: vignette with cupid in flight in the white panel of the middle area. IV style.
21. Room (d), wall O: remains of decoration of the fourth style; in the upper area was a seated female figure.

22. Wing (e), N wall: the fourth style decoration has a low black plinth and a plinth of the same colour, in which panels with stretched garlands and carpet edges alternate with narrow compartments with plants; in the yellow panel in the center of the middle area, now completely vanished, there was a medallion representing a girl with a scroll; other medallions are in the red side panels.

23. Wing (e), N wall, section O: in the medallion, engraved with a compass and bordered by a garland, there was a bust of Satyr (?); The edges of the heart-shaped carpet that delimit the red panel are visible. IV style. 79 N52099
24. Wing(s), S wall with hole left by the passage of ancient prospectors. Decoration of the fourth style with plinth and black plinth; middle area with yellow central panel and red side panels.

25. Wing(s), S wall, E and central section: in the old photo the decoration of the IV style is perfectly preserved. Above a simple black plinth, with panels separated by compartments, the panels of the middle area, bordered by architectural views on a white background, contain medallions with pairs; in the upper white area is a male figure with a palm tree in his left and a crown in his right.
26. Wing (e): the current condition of the medallion reproduced in fig. previous. IV style. 79 N52100
27. Wing(s). In the drawing of G. Discanno (Archive of the German Archaeological Institute) is a medallion with a couple (see fig. 25, left).
28. Wing(s), S wall, section E: detail of the stucco frame with lotuses and trefoils. IV style. 79 N52101

29. Wing (e), S wall, central section: detail of the panel bordered by the edges of a circle carpet, containing a medallion with busts of a couple; in architectural views they are acroterial birds. IV style (from old photo). DAIR W 379
30. Wing (e), S wall, central section: the current condition of the male figure in the upper area (see fig. 25). IV style.

31. Wing (e), wall O: the decoration of the IV style has black plinth and plinth (panels with carpet edges separated by compartments); middle area with yellow central panel (almost completely lost due to the passage into the room of ancient prospectors) and red side panels with vignettes and carpet borders; white upper area and stucco frame.
32. Wing (e), W wall, S section: vignette with cupid in the red middle area. The vignettes were aimed at the painting (?) that was to occupy the center of the back wall of the room. IV style.
33. Wing (e), W wall, N section: vignette with cupid in the red middle area; The edges of the carpet are visible. IV style. '79 N52098
34. Room (f): cocciopesto floor plastered red.

35. Room (f), wall N: overall view of the fourth style decoration. As in the other rooms of the house, these are rather simple decorative schemes: above the discolored plinth, in the center of the middle area is a yellow panel bordered by carpet edges, containing the painting in the center; the side panels with vignettes continue on the adjacent walls; the upper area is discolored, but the light architecture that encloses figures in flight can be recognized. The wall is concluded by a red and green stucco frame, with lotuses and palmettes. 79 N52949
36. Room (f), N wall, section O: detail of the edges of the carpet — not particularly well executed — in squares divided by diagonals. IV style.

37. Room (f), N wall, O section; detail of the upper area, of which we can no longer distinguish the background color, but we can read the decorative motifs with sufficient clarity: a situla, inside an aedicule is a cupid in flight; edges of carpet in semicircles and frame of polychrome stucco with lotuses and palmettes. IV style. 79 N52954
38. Room (f), N wall, section O: upper area with cupid in flight inside a light aedicule. IV style.
39. Room (f), N wall, section O: the red and green stucco frame retains the imprint of the mould, which included the palmette in the centre and half of the lotus flower on each side. IV style.

40. Room (f), N wall, central section. The painting, which depicted a Maenad and a Satyr, was executed on a different layer from that of the surrounding wall, which filled the recess made for this purpose in the now dry plaster. The painting was therefore executed at different times (and by different painters?) than the surrounding wall. IV style.
41. The reproduction of the painting in fig. previous (drawing by Discanno, Archivio Istituto Archeologico Germanico).
42. Room (f), wall E with the door open to the atrium: remains of decoration of the fourth style. '79 N52950
43. Room (f), N wall, section E: the vignette of the white panel of the middle area, with cupid in flight. IV style. 79 N52943
44. Room (f), wall E, section N: in the white panel of the middle area there is a vignette with Maenad in flight. IV style.

45. Room (f), wall S: decoration of the fourth style with discoloured plinth, middle area with yellow central panel with painting and white side panels with vignettes continuing on the adjacent walls; white upper area with polychrome stucco architecture and frame.
46. Room (f), wall S, section E: polychrome stucco frame with lotuses and palmettes. IV style.
47. Room (f), S wall, central section: edges of a semicircular carpet. IV style. 79 N52081

48. Room (f), S wall, central section. This painting, depicting Ganymede sleeping with Zeus' eagle on the right, was also executed — like the others in this room — on a specially prepared layer of plaster. IV style. 79 N52106
49. Discanno's reproduction of the painting in fig. previous (Archive of the German Archaeological Institute). DAIR 58.1917
50. Room (f), wall W with lunette and decoration of the fourth style with central painting. '79 N52063
51. Room (f), wall O, central section: the în situ remains of the painting depicting Narcissus seated in the company of a cupid; this painting is also executed on a layer of plaster. IV style.
52. The reproduction (of Discanno; cf. Disegnatori, p. 847, fig. 12) of the painting in fig. previous.
53. Room (f), wall O, central section: the red and green stucco frame that concludes the upper area, and the lotus and shell frame that concludes the lunette. IV style. '79 N52953

54. Room (g), N wall, IV style decoration: the panels of the red plinth are separated by narrow compartments with plants; in the white panels of the middle area there were vignettes with cupids; upper white area; stucco frame.
55. Room (g), N wall, central section: in the upper white area, a bandage with fringes hangs from two oblique thyrsis on which a bird rests. IV style.
56. Room (g), N wall, section E: narrow compartment with plants in the red plinth, surmounted by a white frieze with dentils. IV style.
57. Room (g), N wall, section E: in the upper white area, within an aedicule surmounted by a small picture with a still life (pomegranates), there is a female figure with a cornucopia. IV style.
58. Room (g), N wall, section E, upper white area: above a candelabrum rests the globe, from which two garlands hang. IV style.
59. Room (g), wall E
60. Room (g), wall E, section N: yellow and purple stucco frame with lotuses and trefoils. IV style.
61. Room (g), S. Also on this wall the decoration of the IV style is preserved in a very poor state.

62. Room (g), wall O with the atrium door: remains of decoration of the fourth style; in the white panels of the middle area were vignettes with cupids. On the edge of the dolio a rectangular stamp with raised letters [Phileros/M(arci) Fulvi ser(vus)].

63. Wing (h), N wall, W section, with two ancient holes. In the black plinth there are panels interspersed with narrow compartments; the middle area has a yellow central panel and a red side panel, separated by architectural views; the upper area is only partially preserved. IV style.
64. Wing (h), N wall, section E: in the upper area there was a small picture with a still life with a diptych containing an inscription. IV style.
65. The decoration of fig. in a reproduction of Discanno (cf. Disegnatori, p. 847, fig. 13).
66. Wing (h), N face, section O: in the black plinth, within a lozenge formed by edges of carpet with two parallel lines, it is a swan in flight. IV style. '79 N52080
67. Wing (h), N wall: in the centre of the middle area there is the sketch graffiti of the cartoon with cupid. IV style.
68. Wing (h), N face, central section: vignette with cupid in flight with torch on the right. IV style.
69. Wing (h), N wall, section E: under the square holes of the floor beams there is a stucco frame with tongues and palmettes. IV style.
70. Wing (h), wall E: remains of decoration of the fourth style. 479 N52050
71. Of the wall reproduced in fig. This female figure was part of the previous one, here in the reproduction by Nicola La Volpe, from 1870. (cf. Draftsmen, p. 758, fig. 230).
73. Wing (h), S wall, O section: IV style decoration. '79 N52052

72. Wing (h), S wall, section E: black plinth (panels separated by narrow compartments with plants); middle area (panels with vignettes separated by narrow compartments with candelabras, closed by partitions); in the upper white area were a standing cupid and a still life with triptych. IV style. 79 N52051
75. Room (i), N wall, section O: in the upper white area there is a female figure with her right hand on her head within a stylized aedicule. IV style.

74. Room (i), N wall with the lunette surmounted by the holes for fixing the false vault. Even the large room that overlooks a corner of the atrium, to the side of the tablinum, has — like all the others in this house — a decoration of the fourth style of modest level.
76. Room (i), wall N: reproduction of the wall shown in fig. 74.
77. Room (i), N wall, central section: red panel with garlands stretched in the plinth. IV style.

78. Room (i): the painting in the centre of the N wall, also executed — like others in this house — on a specially prepared layer of plaster, depicted a male figure with a torch and an inverted urn on the ground, resting on a small pillar (Hermaphrodite?: cf. Schefold VP, pp. 1721'73). IV style.
79. The reproduction of the painting in fig. in a drawing by G. Discanno (Archivio Istituto Archeologico Germanico).
80. Room (i), wall N, central section and E: figures within stucco architecture and cornices; in the white lunette it was a peacock. IV style.
81. Room (i), N wall, central section: Satyr in flight in the upper white area. IV style.
82. Room (i), wall E, section N: remains of a fresco of the fourth style.
83. Room (i), wall E, section N: in the red panel, within a lozenge recess specially made in the plaster, a cupid was painted. IV style.
84. Room (i), wall E, section N: in the yellow panel, on a painting made on a layer of plaster, a cupid hunter was painted. IV style.
85. The painting with the hunter cupid in fig. previous in the reproduction by G. Discanno (Archivio Istituto Archeologico Germanico).

86. Room (i), wall E, section S: remains of a fresco of the fourth style. On this wall, as on almost all walls of the house, the surface of the plaster has been preserved, but it has completely lost its color.
87. Room (i), wall E, section S: the painting with the hunter's cupid that adorned the panel reproduced in fig. is illegible. IV style.
88. Reproduction by G. Discanno (Archive of the German Archaeological Institute) of the painting in fig. previous. DAIR 53.606
89. Room (i), wall E, section S: cupid painted in the red panel, within a lozenge recess made in the plaster. IV style.

90. Room (i): also on the S wall, above a partially walled window, the lunette is preserved. On the wall, the remains of frescoes of the fourth style bear the sign of the passage of people who entered this room — as in the rest of the house — after the eruption. Mau (Mau, in BdI, 1879, p. 193) indicates on this wall the remains of an older decoration, datable to the second style.
92. Room (i), wall W, section N with masonry in opus incerta and head of mixed work (a row of limestone blocks mixed with two brick recurrences): remains of decoration of the IV style.

91. Room (i), wall O, section S: plinth with red central panel with stretched garland and yellow side panels separated by narrow compartments; middle area with yellow central panel and red side panels separated by narrow compartments with a white background closed by partitions; white upper area with carpet architecture and borders. IV style.

93. Room (i), O wall, S section. In the upper white area a series of different ornaments crowd in: a vase inside a shrine, edges of carpet in semicircles, a swan in flight; the molded stucco frame is partially visible. IV style.
94. Room (k): remains of the papier-mâché floor. 79 N52971

95. Room (k), wall N: the decoration in the fourth style of the room (from an old photo from around 1880). The short wall is divided into two parts by a large compartment with a white background, on the side of which the two panels, also white, contain vignettes; the upper area is also white.
96. Room (k), wall N: the current condition of the wall reproduced in fig. previous; On this wall too, the surface of the plaster has remained sufficiently intact, but the color has a lot of
97. Room (k), N wall, section O: the right panel preserves on a white background the sketch of the Muse with zither (Terpsichore), above which there are very few remains of colour. IV style.
98. Room (k), N wall, section O: in the upper white area it is difficult to read a cupid with a torch within an architecture. IV style.
99. Room (k), N wall, central section: the architectural view with coffered and valley, crossed by a candelabrum. IV style.
100. Room (k), N wall, section E: the graffiti sketch of the cartoon with Muse. IV style. '79 N52961

101. Room (k), wall E. In the old photo (circa 1880) we can read the IV style decoration of the room: above a plinth divided into panels and compartments, the middle area has white panels (the central one takes the form of a stretched carpet) with vignettes; in the upper white area there are different ornaments; the wall is concluded by the stucco frame.
102. Room (k): the painted wall reproduced in fig. previous one is now unrecognizable.
103. Room (k), wall E, section N: the panel with cupid in the white panel of the middle area, perfectly identifiable in the photo on fig. 101, has practically disappeared. IV style.

104. Room (k), wall E, central section: in the plinth an oscillum hangs from a double-arched garland, between dolphins and stretched garlands; the carpet bordered by a garland that adorns the middle area is visible. IV style.
105. Room (k), wall E, central section: remains of the Muse with scroll reproduced in fig. 101. IV style.
106. Room (k), wall E, section S: the sketch graffiti of the Muse with mask on the left reproduced in fig. 101. IV style.
107. Room (k), wall S: the decoration of the fourth style, legible only in the old photo dating back to about 1880, is on the whole not very demanding.
108. Room (k), S wall with window: remains of the fourth style decoration reproduced in fig. previous.
109. Room (k), S wall, section O: the sketch of a Muse with two long shins. IV style.

110. Room (k): the old photo, from around 1880, reproduces the O wall with the lunette. The IV style decoration with a white background with vignettes in the panels of the middle area continues the theme of the Muses chosen to decorate this room.
111. Room (k), wall O: the current condition of the wall reproduced in fig. previous. IV style.
113. Room (k), wall O, central section: Muse with zither (sketch graffito). IV style.
112. Room (k), O wall, section S: remains of the vignette with Muse with tragic mask on the right. IV style.
114. Room (k), wall W, section N: stucco frame with lotuses and corollas (the mould included a corolla in the centre, half of the lotus flower on the sides) and halotes and clovers. IV style.

115. Tablinum (l), wall E. The old photo, which dates back to around 1880, reproduces the decoration of the fourth style: in the red plinth, panels alternate with compartments; the middle area has a blue panel in the center — a color not commonly used between two red panels; in the cartoons armed heroes on a shelf. DAIR 53.615
116. Tablinum (1): the E wall has lost all the details of the IV style decoration.
117. Tablinum (l), wall E, section N: in the red plinth there are typical motifs of the IV style, the hanging mask and the edges of a triangle carpet.
118. Tablinum (1), wall E, section N: vignette with armed male figure on a shelf (see fig. 115). IV style.
119. Tablinum (1), wall E, central section: vignette with armed figure (from old photo, circa 1880). IV style.
120. Tablinum (l), wall E, section S: narrow compartment with a swan in the red plinth. IV style.

121. Tablinum (l), wall O: remains of decoration of the fourth style with vignettes with figures of armed men on a shelf; in the center, the sign of the passage of people who penetrated the environment after the eruption.
123. Tablinum (1), wall O, section N: sketch of the cartoon representing an armed figure on a shelf. IV style.
122. Tablinum (l), wall W, central section: in the panel of the red plinth hangs a rhytòn between the edges of a square carpet. IV style.

124. Fauces (m), wall E: the service corridor between the front part of the house, centred on the atrium, and the rear part, centred on the peristyle, also has a wall covering coeval with those of the rest of the house, but even simpler, with red panels in the middle area.

125. Peristyle (n), view from N-E: the columns were covered with black stucco at the bottom (up to a height of 108 cm: Mau, in BdI, 1879, p. 195) and white at the top and joined by a podium painted red on the outside, black on the inside of the peristyle.
126. Room (p), wall N: remains of a decoration of the fourth style, with a red plinth, middle area with traces of fire (which have changed the yellow colour of the panel to red?).
127. Room (p), wall E with the door open to the peristyle: red plinth and middle area with panel of unspecified colour. IV style.
128. Room (p), S wall with remains of a fresco of the fourth style. 79 N52059
129. Room (p), wall O: red plinth and middle area with yellow panels. 79 N52058

1. The vestibule (a) of the entrance at no. 14, open onto the alley that runs along the E side of the insula, is paved with a carpet of white tesserae arranged in a straight warp with a high border of black tesserae; in the foreground the threshold on the street, in lava with recesses for the hinges. In the background, the threshold that marks the entrance to the atrium (b), also in black and white mosaic, whose simple ornamentation with opposing volutes suggests a dating to the Augustan age. (III style).
2. Vestibule (b): threshold towards the atrium, in black and white mosaic with ornamentation with opposing volutes (partly restored). III style.
3. Atrium (b), wall N, to W of the door of (£): in the black plinth, almost completely collapsed, the ornate parts, a rhombus and a band with carpet edges have been preserved. IV style.

4. Atrium (b), wall N, between the doors of (f) and (e): the decoration of the fourth style adapts to the dimensions of the vast room; above a plinth with plants, the middle area has a large central compartment with an architectural glimpse and red side panels, unfortunately very poorly preserved. 79 N53058

5. Atrium (b), wall E, section N with the door of (c). As in the nearby house IX 5, llein many of the houses of this insula (cf. Mau, cited in bibl.) the decoration of the fourth style [here consisting of a black plinth (?) with plants above which, in the red middle area, there is a narrow compartment with a candelabra] covers a masonry in opus incerta with jambs in opus mixed-work (rows of limestone, tuff or lava blocks alternate with two brick recurrences). '79 N53060

6. Atrium (b), wall E, N of the door of (c). The black plinth with plants of the fourth style wall decoration rests on the oldest floor (second style, Republican age), in cocciopesto with ornamentation outlined in black and white tesserae: a dotted with crosses of white tesserae with a central black tile is bordered by a row of white tesserae spaced out and bedded at each corner.
7. Atrium (b), corner N-0, between the doors of (k) and (f): the miserable în situ remains of the fourth style decoration, with a black plinth and a middle area with red panels.
8. Atrium (b), wall W to N of the door of (k): in the plinth you can recognize a small picture with a flower. IV style.

9. Atrium-(B, overall view from S-0: in the old photo (1879) you can recognize the cocciopesto floor with dotted with crosses, the remains of the marble covering of the impluvium with the cistern mouth open on the W side and, on the N wall, the fresco of the IV style.
10. Similar to that of the atrium (b) is the floor of the cubicle (c), which here, however, alternates single white tiles with the crosses; this floor can also be assigned to the II style. 79 N53053

11. Cubicle (c): on the N wall the decoration of the fourth style, effective, but not particularly cared for, is marked by the large hole that was made in the masonry to penetrate the room after the eruption. The plinth has large faux marble panels, the middle area has a large aedicule with a red background in the center with a cusped roof supported by twisted candelabra; the side panels are also red, bordered by carpet edges and containing vignettes.

12. Cubicle (c), N wall: the upper area is also visible here, also red and adorned with garlands, low candelabras, aedicules. The simple molded stucco frame is perhaps older than the fresco of the fourth style.

13. Cubicle (c), N wall, section W; above a low plinth, the faux marble decoration takes up the scansion in panels and compartments typical of the IV style: on the left a rhomboidal tile imitating antique yellow marble is inserted within porphyry elements; on the right, two triangular tiles of the same marble are faced with two porphyry tiles.
14. Cubicle (c), N wall, central section: the painting shows the subject, very frequent in cubicles decorated in the IV style, of the (Venus?) Fisherwoman surrounded by cupids.
15. The reproduction of the painting in fig. in a drawing by the German Archaeological Institute.

16. Cubicle (c), wall E: in the lunette there is a high window overlooking the alley. Fourth style decoration with faux marble plinth, middle area with central aedicule and side panels with vignettes, red upper area. The painting in the center of this wall also contained a 'fisherwoman'.
17. Cubicle (c), wall E, section N: detail of the simple moulded stucco cornices that define the lunette. 79 N53056
18. Cubicle (c), S wall with fresco of the fourth style.

19. Cubicle (c), S wall: in the upper area, also red, is a small picture with dolphins, surmounted by a pair of candelabra supporting a triple-arched garland. The decorative motifs, typical of the IV style, are almost completely lost; the simple stucco molded frame is perhaps older.

20. Cubicle (c), S wall, central section: the painting with Hero and Leander has some characteristics in common with the painting of the same subject in the House of the Vettii, VI 15, 1 (cf. vol. V, pp. 484-485, fig. 25). IV style.
21. In the panel by G. Discanno (cf. Draftsmen, p. 845, fig. 10) it is possible to recognize some details of the painting in fig. previous: Leandro swims below, while Ero
22. Cubicle (c), S wall, central section: detail of the upper area. IV style.

23. Cubicle (c), wall O with the door open to the atrium (b): imitation marble plinth, yellow middle area with vignettes and carpet edges; remains of decoration of the fourth style in the upper red area. IV style.

24. Cubicle (d), N wall with the lunette and the holes to which the reed of the false vault was attached. The decoration of the fourth style is much less preserved here than in the adjoining cubicle (c): above a faux marble plinth, in the center of the middle area, there is a large yellow compartment with a candelabrum; the side panels are red, the upper area white.
25. Cubicle (d), N wall, section E: detail of the red panel vignette, with a swan in flight. IV style.

26. Cubicle (d), wall E with high window open onto the alley. The decoration of the fourth style is very simple: above the plinth, the plinth has faux marble panels alternating with compartments; the middle area has a large yellow compartment in the center in which there is a candelabra, on the sides red panels bordered by edges of triangle carpet; the upper area is discolored.
27. Cubicle (d), S wall: the state of conservation of the fourth style decoration, here a little better than on the other walls, allows us to assess its very modest level.
28. Cubicle (d), O wall to N of the door open to the atrium (b): in the yellow compartment the twisted candelabra was painted very quickly. IV style.

1. Façade, pillar O: detail of the upper area with a white background with a distilo temple from whose small cella Mercury emerged, stationary in the pronaos. The god wears a white tunic with a dark cloak, winged sandals and yellow petasus; in his right hand he holds the pouch and in the left the caduceus. The final part of the electoral inscription for Iulius Polybius and Holconius Priscus is visible at the top; the underlying scene of the sale of felt shoes is only partially filmed, the impilia that the seller shows to the customer of whom only the head can be seen on the right.

2. Façade, pillar E: Pompeian Venus on the quadriga pulled by elephants, flanked by Fortuna and the Genius (who for this very reason are to be referred to the city itself), dominates, in a balanced and symmetrical composition, closed at the top by hanging garlands, finely cared for in the rendering of all the details, over the underlying scene of production and exhibition of the products of the workshop,  from which it is separated by the moulded frame.

3. Façade, pillar E: detail of the upper area on a white background. Venus, with turreted crown, earrings, necklace and rings, in a purple robe, stands upright, leaning on a rudder with her left hand in which she also holds the sceptre, in a chariot shaped like the bow of a ship and adorned with elements defined by some as "sirens" by others as "anchors". Next to her is Eros, crowned with leaves and in a yellow cloak, who raises a circular mirror aloft. On the sides fly two naked cupids carrying a garland and a palm branch. The reference to the oriental tradition of the royal chariots pulled by these animals is evident, with an implicit reference to the richness of those lands that can only be brought to the small Vesuvian city by its patron deity. 4. Façade, pillar E: in the predella below the tutelary deity, there is an interesting depiction of different phases of the work that took place in the workshop. In the background we see three characters seated behind low banquets, carding on high wooden planks ending with combs the wool or hair from which to obtain the felt. In the center is represented the moment of the actual "dough", carried out by the four bare-chested workers, near the furnace, while on the far right there is Verecundus, as the name written below indicates. They have been observed wearing loose robes, probably to protect themselves from the fur residues that rose into the air during processing.

6. Façade, pillar E, central section: detail of the scene of kneading the fleeces with coagulating substances, such as vinegar. The four workers, with robust but harmonious shapes and well rendered in proportions, covered only by loincloths, press and twist in triangular basins, resting on trestles near the mouth of a boiler, the felts. 1. Triclinium (5), N wall, central section: of the painting with Galatea and Polyphemus only the drawing of the German Archaeological Institute remains; from Mau's description we deduce the colors of the clothes of the two characters, which were yellow for the robe resting on the arm of Polyphemus seated on a rock near the sea, and purplish red for the mantle of Galatea who holds on to the neck of the hippocampus on which she is seated to sail the sea. The scene is the usual one of the Oceanina watched by the gigantic shepherd, who is in love with her; The two sheep and the ram, which in Mediterranean countries also graze near the sea, complete, as in other replicas of the same subject, the composition. DAIR 53.592

2. Triclinium (5), wall O: the drawing of the German Archaeological Institute documents the painting with Diana and Actaeon. The goddess who, having laid her clothes on a rock, is about to take a bath by a stream in a rocky cave, is surprised by the hunter who looks at her in admiration, emerging behind the rocks, while she raises her threatening right hand towards him, and with her left hand covers her chest. On the right there is a base on which three statuettes rest. It is one of the many replicas of the subject, widely spread in the III and IV styles, in which only the moment of surprise, and therefore of the outrage against the goddess and not that of punishment, is treated. The presence of the statuettes on the pillar, which almost has the function of an altar, accentuates in a certain sense the sacred character of the goddess's bath.

Cubicle (a), wall O, central section: the painting (0.98 x 0.74), in the Museum of Naples (inv. 120176) from 1 October 1890, is one of the most vivid depictions of the last night of Troy, all the more dramatic as it depicts the moment when the festive crowd welcomes the horse within the walls. The compact mass of the Trojans, willing to create a corridor in continuation of the demolished walls, is contrasted by a large female figure who, in the distance, threateningly waves two torches: probably Cassandra who presages the tragic end of the city. The impressionistic execution of the figures painted with sure touches of color to which almost nothing is added by the drawing of details, whether they are still figures or the very lively ones of the dancers in the foreground, and the meandering movement of the procession, contribute to giving the sensation of a whirlwind that is about to overwhelm everything; The abundant use of white is intended to achieve the effect of moonlight.
